nl.statement: Fix the finite supports \(\mathcal X,\mathcal A\), carrying their intended discrete/Borel measurable structures, the known feature map \(\phi\), the known reference and logging policy \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\), and \(\eta\) as \(\mathfrak E=(\mathcal X,\mathcal A,\phi,\pi_{\mathrm{ref}},\eta)\). The context distribution \(\rho\) is not a component of \(\mathfrak E\); it remains law-specific. For every compatible one-observation law \(P\), \(\mathcal D_n\sim P^{\otimes n}\). A learner is an element of \(\mathcal L_n(\mathfrak E)\), so it receives \(\mathcal D_n\) and \(\mathfrak E\), returns a policy, and is supported on \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\) at every context. Because \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\) is public, this support requirement is law-independent and uses only public design inputs. By \(\text{def:minimax-risk}\), it is without loss relative to the class of all measurable full-simplex policy learners under the extended reverse-KL convention. Write \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\), \(\mathfrak R_{n,\mathfrak E}\), and \(N^\star_{\mathfrak E}\) whenever public experiments are compared. The unindexed notation \(\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\), \(\mathfrak R_n\), and \(N^\star\) is an abbreviation only after one \(\mathfrak E\) has been fixed and no cross-experiment comparison is being made.

nl.statement:
Let \(S=\mathcal X\times\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal F=\{f\in[0,1]^S:\exists\theta\in\mathbb R^d,\ f(x,a)=\phi(x,a)^\top\theta\}\). Fix once and for all a lexicographic order of \(S\). Set \(L_n(f)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(Y_i-f(X_i,A_i))^2\), and let \(\widehat f\) be the sequentially lexicographically selected minimizer of \(L_n\) over the compact polytope \(\mathcal F\). Define \(\|h\|_n^2=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nh(X_i,A_i)^2\) and \(\mathcal Q_n=\{f\in\mathcal F:\|f-\widehat f\|_n^2\le c_0[d\log(en)+\log(2n^2)]/n\}\). The set \(\mathcal Q_n\) is nonempty and compact because it contains \(\widehat f\). For every \((x,a)\in S\), define the unique minimum value \(\underline r_n(x,a)=\min_{f\in\mathcal Q_n}f(x,a)\); if an attaining witness is needed, select one sequentially lexicographically using the fixed order of \(S\). Define the deployed policy at every context, observed or unobserved, by
\[
\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x)e^{\eta\underline r_n(x,a)}}{\sum_{b\in\mathcal A}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(b\mid x)e^{\eta\underline r_n(x,b)}}.
\]
This Gibbs policy satisfies \(\operatorname{supp}\widehat\pi(\cdot\mid x)=\operatorname{supp}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid x)\) for every context and therefore belongs to the finite-objective decision class. For reference-supported policies \(\pi\), retain \(\underline J_n(\pi)=\inf_{f\in\mathcal Q_n}[n^{-1}\sum_i\sum_a\pi(a\mid X_i)f(X_i,a)-(\eta n)^{-1}\sum_i\operatorname{KL}(\pi(\cdot\mid X_i)\Vert\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid X_i))]\) as the empirical pessimistic criterion; no real-valued off-support evaluation is intended. In any feature coordinates, \(\|f_\theta-f_{\widehat\theta}\|_n^2=(\theta-\widehat\theta)^\top\widehat\Sigma_n(\theta-\widehat\theta)\), where \(\widehat\Sigma_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\phi(X_i,A_i)\phi(X_i,A_i)^\top\); this equality is notation only and no coefficient representative is selected.

review.note: Unfolding all fields gives exactly the bounded linear prediction class, lexicographically selected squared-loss ERM, empirical confidence polytope, coordinatewise minimum via sInf, Gibbs deployment on every context, and supported-policy pessimistic criterion; compactness/nonemptiness makes the totalized choices and sInf extensionally equal to the stated minima.

nl.statement:
For a fixed public experiment \(\mathfrak E\) and every nonempty class \(\mathcal M\) of laws compatible with \(\mathfrak E\), use the standard extended reverse-KL convention in \(J_{\eta,P}\). Thus a policy that assigns positive mass outside \(\operatorname{supp}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid x)\) at any context with positive \(\rho\)-mass has objective \(-\infty\) and regret \(+\infty\). For an arbitrary policy \(\pi\), define the public contextwise support repair
\[
(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{ref}}\pi)(a\mid x)=
\begin{cases}
\pi(a\mid x),&\pi(b\mid x)=0\text{ for every }b\text{ such that }\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(b\mid x)=0,\\
\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x),&\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]
Because the supports have the standing finite discrete/Borel measurable structures, \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{ref}}\) is Borel measurable and sends every measurable policy learner to an element of \(\mathcal L_n(\mathfrak E)\). For every law and every realized learner output, its repair leaves the objective unchanged when every offending context has zero \(\rho\)-mass, while otherwise the unrepaired regret is \(+\infty\) and the repaired regret is finite. Hence repair never increases regret. Since supported learners are themselves full-simplex learners, the two infima are equal, and their common value is
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,\mathfrak E}(\mathcal M)=\inf_{\widetilde\pi\in\mathcal L_n(\mathfrak E)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[J_{\eta,P}(\pi_P^\star)-J_{\eta,P}(\widetilde\pi(\mathcal D_n;\mathfrak E))\right].
\]
Equivalently, the right-hand side equals the same infimum taken over all measurable full-simplex policy-valued learners with the displayed loss interpreted in \([0,+\infty]\). The Gibbs optimum has exactly the support of \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\), and the public reference learner has finite regret, so the common minimax value is a nonnegative real number. When \(\mathfrak E\) is fixed and no experiments are compared, write \(\mathfrak R_n=\mathfrak R_{n,\mathfrak E}\).

review.note: On the note's nonempty-model domain, unfolding `Learner`, `IsMeasurableLearner`, and `learnerRisk` gives exactly the infimum over measurable reference-supported learners of the worst-law expected regularized regret; the full-simplex formulation is the equivalent support-repair presentation.

nl.statement:
For \((C,D)\in\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{hard}}^\circ(d,\eta)\), put \(k=\lfloor(d-1)/2\rfloor\), take an orthonormal basis \(e_0,(u_j,w_j)_{j=1}^k\), and add \(z\) when \(d\) is even. Use actions \(\{+,-,0\}\). At \(x_C\), set \(q=(e^\eta/C-1)/(e^\eta-1)\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(+\mid x_C)=q\), distribute \(1-q\) positively over \(-,0\), and set \(\phi(x_C,+)=e_0\), \(\phi(x_C,-)=\phi(x_C,0)=0\), and \(\theta_0=1\). Put \(A=q(C-D)/(D-1)\), add \(x_A\) when \(C>D\) with every action feature equal to \(e_0\), give \(x_C\) raw mass \(\tau=[4(1+A)]^{-1}\) and \(x_A\) raw mass \(\tau A\), and give the hard contexts total raw mass one. When \(z\) is present, add \(x_z\) with raw mass \(1/4\), every action feature \(z\), and coefficient zero. Normalize these raw masses to define \(\rho\). At each \(x_j\), of raw mass \(1/k\), put \(p=(4D)^{-1}\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(+\mid x_j)=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(-\mid x_j)=p\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(0\mid x_j)=1-2p\), \(\phi(x_j,+)=(u_j+w_j)/\sqrt2\), \(\phi(x_j,-)=(u_j-w_j)/\sqrt2\), and \(\phi(x_j,0)=0\). For \(v\in\{-1,1\}^k\), let \(T_\gamma=D(1-2p)/[e^{\eta\gamma}-2pD\cosh(\eta\gamma)]\), \(\beta=\eta^{-1}\log T_\gamma\), and \(\theta_{u_j}=\sqrt2\beta\), \(\theta_{w_j}=\sqrt2\gamma v_j\), so \(r_v(x_j,\pm)=\beta\pm\gamma v_j\). Define
\[
g_0(D,\eta)=\sup\left\{g>0:\text{ for every }s\in[0,g],\ e^{\eta s}-2pD\cosh(\eta s)>0\text{ and }s\le\eta^{-1}\log T_s\le1-s\right\},
\]
and set \(\gamma(\epsilon,d,C,D,\eta)=\eta^{-1}\operatorname{arcosh}(e^{64\eta\epsilon})\). The family \(\mathcal H_{d,C,D,\eta,\epsilon}\) comprises these \(2^k\) Bernoulli laws whenever \(\gamma\le\min\{g_0(D,\eta),1/4,\beta,1-\beta\}\).

Using the sequentially lexicographically selected empirical-risk minimizer \(\widehat f\in\mathcal F\) from \(\text{def:prediction-polytope-learner}\), define, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(a\in\mathcal A\),
\[
\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{ERM}}(a\mid x)
=\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x)e^{\eta\widehat f(x,a)}}{\sum_{b\in\mathcal A}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(b\mid x)e^{\eta\widehat f(x,b)}}.
\]
The learner receives only \((\mathcal D_n,\mathfrak E)\); it does not receive the shell indices \(C\) or \(D\).

nl.statement:
There are universal constants such that, after choosing \(c_0\) sufficiently large and whenever \(\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\ne\varnothing\), the lower-envelope Gibbs learner \(\widehat\pi\in\mathcal L_n(\mathfrak E)\) uses neither \(C\) nor \(D\) as input and satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[J_{\eta,P}(\pi_P^\star)-J_{\eta,P}(\widehat\pi)]
\le\widetilde O\left(\min\left\{\frac{\eta d^2D}{n},\sqrt{\frac{d^2D}{n}}\right\}\right)+\delta_n.
\]
The proof derives a distribution-free \(d/n\) logging prediction radius for every member of \(\mathcal Q_n\), a pointwise leverage majorant for the nonlinear lower envelope, the trace inequality \(D_{2,P}\le dD_P\), the Gibbs regret identity, and the endpoint-monotonicity fast and slow conversions. Consequently
\[
N^\star(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)
\le\widetilde O\left(d^2D\min\{\eta/\epsilon,\epsilon^{-2}\}\right)
\]
when the right-hand side is at least two. The additional factor \(d\) is unavoidable for the empirical-ball lower-envelope learner in general: \(\text{prop:empirical-ball-dimension-witness}\) gives exact shells on which the original \(dD\) upper rate fails.

Its members satisfy exactly \(C_P=C\), \(D_P=D\), and \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\succ0\). There are constants \(\epsilon_1(C,D,\eta)\in(0,\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)]\) and \(c(C,D,\eta)>0\) such that, for every \(0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_1(C,D,\eta)\), \(N^\star(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)\ge c(C,D,\eta)dD\eta/\epsilon\). nl.statement:
Let \(\mathcal G\subseteq[0,1]^S\), let \(W_1,\ldots,W_n\) be independent with common law \(\mu\), and let \(N_{\mathcal G}(u)\) be the \(u\)-covering number of \(\mathcal G\) in supremum norm. For \(0<u<1\), with probability at least \(1-\delta\), simultaneously for every \(g_1,g_2\in\mathcal G\),
\[
\mathbb E_\mu(g_1-g_2)^2
\le \frac2n\sum_{i=1}^n(g_1-g_2)^2(W_i)
+\frac{32}{3n}\log\frac{2N_{\mathcal G}(u)}{\delta}+10u.
\]

nl.statement:

If \(\Pi\) is a \(\mathcal G\)-measurable orthogonal projector of rank at most \(d\), then, conditionally with probability at least \(1-\zeta\),
\[

\le8\left\{d\log5+\log\frac2\zeta\right\}.
\]

nl.statement: Let \((\Omega,\Sigma)\) be a measurable space, let \(K\) be a separable metrizable space, let \(\Gamma:\Omega\rightrightarrows K\) be weakly measurable with nonempty compact values, and let \(u:\Omega\times K\to\mathbb R\) be measurable in its first argument and continuous in its second. nl.statement:
For the lower-envelope Gibbs completion of the empirical ball in \(\text{def:prediction-polytope-learner}\), the claimed \(\widetilde O(dD/n)\) fast rate is false. Specifically, fix \(\eta_0=4\log3\), \(C_0=3/2\), and \(D_0=13/10\). There is a sequence of public experiments and deterministic-reward laws \(P_d\in\mathcal M(d,C_0,D_0,\eta_0)\) such that, for \(n_d=\lceil d^2\rceil\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_d^{\otimes n_d}}[J_{\eta_0,P_d}(\pi_{P_d}^\star)-J_{\eta_0,P_d}(\widehat\pi)]
\ge \frac{\log(4/3)}{8\log3}\{1-o(1)\}.
\]
In contrast, both \(dD_0/n_d\) and \(\sqrt{dD_0/n_d}\) tend to zero up to polylogarithmic factors.

review.note: After unfolding ExactShell, learnerRisk, and lowerEnvelopePolicy, Lean gives the c₀=64 empirical-ball Gibbs learner, exact constants η₀=4 log 3, C₀=3/2, D₀=13/10, deterministic rewards, n_d=d²=⌈d²⌉, and the paper proof's explicit error d·exp(-d(3 log 3-2))=o(1); the two stated Tendsto formulas are D₀/d and √(D₀/d), which also vanish after any fixed polylogarithmic factor.

nl.statement: For every nonempty exact shell, \(1\le D\le C\le e^\eta\); because the supports are finite, either \((C,D)=(1,1)\) or \(1<D\le C<e^\eta\). Conversely, for every \(d\ge4\) and every pair \(1<D\le C<e^\eta\), there is a finite public experiment with bounded features and nonsingular logging covariance for which \(\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\ne\varnothing\); the pair \((1,1)\) is also realizable. Thus the feasible index region when the public experiment may vary is exactly \(\{(1,1)\}\cup\{(C,D):1<D\le C<e^\eta\}\). Feasibility for a fixed public experiment can be strictly smaller: canonical tabular features force \(D=C\), whereas shared features realize off-diagonal pairs \(D<C\). This theorem answers the feasibility part of the question; it does not assert a minimax lower frontier outside the proved local hard regime.

review.note: After unfolding CommonExperiment, ExactShell, and IsCanonicalTabular, the five Lean conjuncts exactly encode the strict feasible-region necessity, interior and boundary realizability for d≥4 at fixed η, canonical-tabular diagonal restriction D=C, and shared noncanonical off-diagonal realizability.

nl.statement:
For every \(d\ge4\), \(\eta>0\), and \(1<D\le C<e^\eta\), there is a fixed finite public experiment \(\mathfrak E_1\) with bounded features and a nonempty exact shell \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E_1}(d,C,D,\eta)\), and there are constants \(c(C,D,\eta)>0\) and \(\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)>0\) such that
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E_1}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)\ge c(C,D,\eta)\frac{dD\eta}{\epsilon}
\qquad(0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)).
\]
No condition \(2D-1<e^\eta\) is required. The constants may depend on \((C,D,\eta)\); hence this is a pointwise local \(d/\epsilon\) lower bound with displayed factor \(D\eta\), not a uniform assertion about coverage or temperature dependence.

review.note: The quantifiers make c and eps0 depend only on (C,D,eta), while the finite experiment may depend on d and is fixed across eps; shell nonemptiness unfolds to an exact shell with bounded features, and the natural ceiling bound is equivalent to the displayed real lower bound. The explicit eps<1 restriction is the intrinsic domain of sampleComplexity and is equivalent under the existential eps0 by shrinking eps0 below 1.

nl.statement:
Fix \(c_0=64\), let \(a_n=d\log(en)+\log(2n^2)\), and suppose \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\ne\varnothing\). Let \(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{ERM}}\) be the Gibbs policy generated by \(\widehat f\) as in \(\text{def:erm-gibbs-plugin-learner}\). This learner belongs to \(\mathcal L_n(\mathfrak E)\), uses neither \(C\) nor \(D\) as input, and satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[J_{\eta,P}(\pi_P^\star)-J_{\eta,P}(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{ERM}})]
\le
\min\left\{
600\kappa_\eta\frac{Da_n}{n},
\sqrt{600}(1+e^{2\eta})\sqrt{\frac{Da_n}{n}}
\right\}
+\frac{\delta_n}{2}\min\{2,\eta/2\}.
\]
Consequently, whenever the displayed sample-size order is at least two,
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)
\le\widetilde O\left(
 dD\min\left\{
 \frac{\kappa_\eta}{\epsilon},
 \frac{(1+e^{2\eta})^2}{\epsilon^2}
 \right\}
\right).
\]
Together with \(\text{thm:localized-upper}\), this yields the complementary general envelope
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)
\le\widetilde O\left(
 dD\min\left\{
 \frac{d\eta}{\epsilon},
 \frac d{\epsilon^2},
 \frac{\kappa_\eta}{\epsilon},
 \frac{(1+e^{2\eta})^2}{\epsilon^2}
 \right\}
\right).
\]
No clean-temperature \(\widetilde O(dD\min\{\eta/\epsilon,\epsilon^{-2}\})\) conclusion is asserted.

review.note: Unfolding the referenced definitions, ExactShell E P0 C D witnesses precisely shell nonemptiness, the pointwise ∀P bound is the uniform supremum bound, ermGibbsPluginLearner depends on neither C nor D, and the universal-K ceiling formulas explicitly realize both stated tilde-O sample-complexity envelopes; ZhaoUniformSquareComparison is the directly threaded attested cited interface.

nl.statement:
Fix \(c_0=64\). For every \(P\in\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\) and every \(n\in\mathbb N\), with \(\delta_n=n^{-2}\), there is an event \(\mathcal E_n\) satisfying \(P^{\otimes n}(\mathcal E_n)\ge1-\delta_n/2\) such that
\[
r_\theta\in\mathcal Q_n
\quad\text{and}\quad
\sup_{f\in\mathcal Q_n}\mathbb E_{X\sim\rho,A\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid X)}[(f(X,A)-r_\theta(X,A))^2]
\le600\frac{d\log(en)+\log(2n^2)}{n}.
\]
More generally, for any fixed universal \(c_0\ge64\), the constant \(600\) may be replaced by \(4c_0+291\).

review.note: ExactShell supplies the paper's bounded linear reward and reference-logging law, productLaw is P^{⊗n}, failureProbability is n⁻², and the pointwise-for-all-f conclusion is equivalent to the supremum bound; the general coefficient 4c0+291 also implies the stated c0=64 coefficient 600 because the rate factor is nonnegative.

nl.statement:
Let \(r,g:S\to[0,1]\), put \(\Delta=g-r\), and let \(\pi_r\) and \(\pi_g\) be their Gibbs policies relative to \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\). Write
\[
J_{\eta,r}(\pi)=\mathbb E_{\rho,\pi}r(X,A)-\eta^{-1}\mathbb E_\rho\operatorname{KL}(\pi(\cdot\mid X)\Vert\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid X)),
\]
and define
\[
\kappa_\eta=\eta\int_0^1t e^{2\eta t}\,dt
=\frac{e^{2\eta}(2\eta-1)+1}{4\eta}.
\]
Then
\[
J_{\eta,r}(\pi_r)-J_{\eta,r}(\pi_g)
\le\min\left\{
\kappa_\eta\mathbb E_{\rho,\pi_r}[\Delta^2],
(1+e^{2\eta})\sqrt{\mathbb E_{\rho,\pi_r}[\Delta^2]}
\right\}.
\]

review.note: Unfolding gibbsFromPotential, welfareFromPotential, policyKL, and kappa gives exactly the paper's Gibbs policies, regularized welfare, Delta-squared expectation, and both bounds; the omitted displayed closed form for kappa is algebraically equivalent to its encoded integral because eta>0 is carried by CommonExperiment.

nl.statement:
Fix \(d\ge4\), \(\eta>0\), \(1<D<C<e^\eta\), and any finite public experiment \(\mathfrak E\) for which \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\ne\varnothing\). Define
\[
b_\eta=\frac12\min\{2,\eta/2\},\qquad
Q_{d,D,\eta}=\max\{600\kappa_\eta D(d+2),b_\eta,1\}.
\]
Then, for every \(0<\epsilon<1\),
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)
\le
\left\lceil\frac{8Q_{d,D,\eta}}{\epsilon}
\log\!\left(\frac{8eQ_{d,D,\eta}}{\epsilon}\right)\right\rceil .
\]
Consequently,
\[
\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}
\frac{\epsilon^2}{d}N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=0.
\]
Thus no specified finite public experiment, genuinely shared-feature or otherwise, admits constants \(c(C,D,\eta)>0\) and \(\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)>0\) for which \(N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)\ge c(C,D,\eta)d/\epsilon^2\) for every \(0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)\). The proposed shared-feature slow branch is therefore false.

review.note: After unfolding the referenced definitions, CommonExperiment supplies d≥4 and η>0, hshell witnesses exact-shell nonemptiness, and inversionQ is exactly Q_{d,D,η}; since Q≥1 and d≥4, the displayed O(ε⁻¹ log(1/ε)) ceiling bound implies both the omitted limit and the quadratic-lower-bound negation, while hZhao is the paper's cited background comparison lemma.

nl.statement:
Fix \(d\ge4\), \(\eta>0\), and any finite public experiment \(\mathfrak E\) for which \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\ne\varnothing\). Define
\[
b_\eta=\frac12\min\{2,\eta/2\},\qquad
Q_{d,D,\eta}=\max\{600\kappa_\eta D(d+2),b_\eta,1\}.
\]
Then, for every \(0<\epsilon<1\),
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)
\le
\left\lceil\frac{8Q_{d,D,\eta}}{\epsilon}
\log\!\left(\frac{8eQ_{d,D,\eta}}{\epsilon}\right)\right\rceil .
\]
Consequently,
\[
\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}
\frac{\epsilon^2}{d}N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=0.
\]
Thus no specified finite public experiment with a nonempty exact shell admits constants \(c(C,D,\eta)>0\) and \(\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)>0\) for which \(N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)\ge c(C,D,\eta)d/\epsilon^2\) for every \(0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)\). This is an asymptotic conclusion and does not exclude slower preasymptotic behavior on a restricted accuracy interval.

review.note: Unfolding gives inversionB = ½ min{2,η/2}, inversionQ = max{600 κη D(d+2),bη,1}, the witness P0 with hshell is equivalent to shell nonemptiness, and E carries d≥4, η>0, and finiteness; the first conjunct is exactly the stated ceiling bound, while sampleComplexityReal equals the finite natural sample complexity under that bound, so Tendsto is the stated right-limit, which also logically implies the omitted redundant no-positive-quadratic-lower-bound consequence.

nl.statement: For every \(d\ge4\), \(\eta>0\), and \(1<D\le C<e^\eta\), there is a finite public experiment with bounded features and a nonempty exact shell \(\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\) such that every member of the shell has the same publicly computable Gibbs optimum. For this experiment, \(\mathfrak R_n(\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta))=0\) for every \(n\in\mathbb N\), and \(N^\star(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=1\) for every \(\epsilon>0\).

review.note: After unfolding, nonemptiness of exactShellSet supplies BoundedFeatures for the finite Fin experiment; the common IsPolicy witness is exactly the shell-wide Gibbs optimum, minimaxRisk is the stated inf–sup regret, and sampleComplexityPositive is the infimum over n≥1, so zero risk for every n gives N*=1 for every ε>0.

nl.statement:
For a fixed public experiment \(\mathfrak E\), nonemptiness of \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\) is equivalent to the explicit finite exponential nonlinear-semidefinite feasibility system in \(\text{lem:fixed-experiment-shell-certificate}\). Nevertheless, the indices \((d,C,D,\eta)\) do not determine the fixed-experiment minimax frontier. For every \(d\ge4\), \(\eta>0\), and \(1<D\le C<e^\eta\), there is a finite public experiment \(\mathfrak E_0\) with a nonempty exact \((C,D)\)-shell on which
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,\mathfrak E_0}\bigl(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E_0}(d,C,D,\eta)\bigr)=0
\]
for every \(n\), and \(N^\star_{\mathfrak E_0}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=1\) for every \(\epsilon>0\). There is also a finite public experiment \(\mathfrak E_1\) at the same indices and constants \(c(C,D,\eta)>0\) and \(\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)>0\) for which
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E_1}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)\ge c(C,D,\eta)\frac{dD\eta}{\epsilon}
\qquad(0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)).
\]
These conclusions include pairs satisfying \(2D-1\ge e^\eta\). Consequently, any sample-complexity lower bound that is uniform over all fixed public experiments with a nonempty shell at the given indices is at most \(1\); no nontrivial such bound can exceed the unavoidable inequality \(N^\star_{\mathfrak E}\ge1\), and no such bound can diverge as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\). In particular, no uniform matching \(\Omega(dD\epsilon^{-2})\) branch can hold as a function only of \((d,C,D,\eta)\).

review.note: After unfolding all referenced definitions, Lean gives the certificate equivalence, uniform-in-d zero-risk and informative experiments at every 1 < D ≤ C < exp η, the stated local dDη/ε lower frontier, and the experiment-uniform ceiling of 1; the extra ε < 1 guard is equivalent because the existential positive ε₀ may be decreased below 1.

nl.statement:
Fix the public experiment \(\mathfrak E\), and write \(\mathcal A_x^+=\{a\in\mathcal A:\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x)>0\}\). For \(\vartheta\in\mathbb R^d\), define
\[
Z_\vartheta(x)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x)e^{\eta\phi(x,a)^\top\vartheta},\qquad
w_\vartheta(x,a)=\frac{e^{\eta\phi(x,a)^\top\vartheta}}{Z_\vartheta(x)},
\]
\[
B_x=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x)\phi(x,a)\phi(x,a)^\top,
\qquad
G_x(\vartheta)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(a\mid x)w_\vartheta(x,a)\phi(x,a)\phi(x,a)^\top.
\]
Then \(\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\ne\varnothing\) if and only if the public feature map has Euclidean norm at most one at every cell and at least one of the following finitely many feasibility problems has a solution. Enumerate a nonempty set \(I\subseteq\mathcal X\) and a cell \((x_0,a_0)\) with \(x_0\in I\) and \(a_0\in\mathcal A_{x_0}^+\). The variables are \(\vartheta\in\mathbb R^d\), \((\rho_x)_{x\in I}\), and \(u\in\mathbb R^d\), and the constraints are
\[
0\le\phi(x,a)^\top\vartheta\le1\quad((x,a)\in S),\qquad
\rho_x>0\quad(x\in I),\qquad \sum_{x\in I}\rho_x=1,
\]
\[
B(\rho):=\sum_{x\in I}\rho_xB_x\succ0,
\]
\[
e^{\eta\phi(x,a)^\top\vartheta}\le C Z_\vartheta(x)\quad(x\in I\text{ and }a\in\mathcal A_x^+),
\qquad
e^{\eta\phi(x_0,a_0)^\top\vartheta}=C Z_\vartheta(x_0),
\]
\[
G(\vartheta,\rho):=\sum_{x\in I}\rho_xG_x(\vartheta),\qquad
DB(\rho)-G(\vartheta,\rho)\succeq0,
\]
\[
\{DB(\rho)-G(\vartheta,\rho)\}u=0,\qquad u^\top u=1.
\]
There are at most \((2^{|\mathcal X|}-1)|S|\) branches, and a branch has \(2d+|I|\) real variables and only displayed exponential, linear, quadratic, and semidefinite constraints.

review.note: Unfolding the feasibility system gives exactly the support, positivity, normalization, covariance, Gibbs-ratio, semidefinite, and unit-kernel constraints, while the remaining conjuncts faithfully encode the branch and variable counts.

nl.statement:
Fix \(c_0=64\). For every positive integer \(n\) and \(g,f\in\mathcal F\), let \(\pi_g\) be the Gibbs policy generated by \(g\), and define
\[
H_{g,f}(x)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\pi_g(a\mid x)\{g(x,a)-f(x,a)\}^2,
\qquad
\widehat U_n(g)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal Q_n}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nH_{g,f}(X_i).
\]
Let \(\widetilde g_n\) be the sequentially lexicographically selected member of \(\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{g\in\mathcal Q_n}\widehat U_n(g)\), and let \(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{stab}}=\pi_{\widetilde g_n}\). This is a measurable member of \(\mathcal L_n(\mathfrak E)\), uses only \((\mathcal D_n,\mathfrak E)\), and uses neither \(\rho\), \(C\), nor \(D\) as input. Put
\[
a_n=d\log(en)+\log(2n^2),
\]
\[
b_n=\frac{8}{3n}\left[\log(4n^2)+2d\log\{1+4n(\eta+2)\}\right]+\frac3n,
\qquad
V_n=D\left(3000\frac{a_n}{n}+3b_n\right).
\]
For every nonempty exact shell and every positive integer \(n\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[J_{\eta,P}(\pi_P^\star)-J_{\eta,P}(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{stab}})\right]
\le
\min\left\{\eta V_n,\sqrt{2V_n}\right\}
+\delta_n\min\{2,\eta/2\}.
\]
Moreover, for every \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\), the following explicit inversion holds. If \(\eta\le2\epsilon\), then
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=1.
\]
If \(\eta>2\epsilon\), define
\[
q_\epsilon=dD\min\{\eta/\epsilon,\epsilon^{-2}\},
\qquad
\ell_\epsilon=1+\log(eq_\epsilon)+\log\{1+(1+\eta)q_\epsilon\},
\]
\[
n_0=\left\lceil10^8q_\epsilon\ell_\epsilon\right\rceil.
\]
Then
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n_0}}\left[J_{\eta,P}(\pi_P^\star)-J_{\eta,P}(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{stab}})\right]
\le\epsilon,
\qquad
N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)\le n_0.
\]
Consequently, with universal constants and whenever the displayed sample-size order is at least two,
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)
\le\widetilde O\left(dD\min\{\eta/\epsilon,\epsilon^{-2}\}\right).
\]
Thus the clean feature-coverage upper bound holds at every temperature; pointwise coverage \(C\) is not needed by the learner or by this upper bound.

review.note: After unfolding the stabilized selector, confidence polytope, measurable-learner predicate, exact shell, learner risk, failure schedule, variance radius, q/log factors, and sample complexity, Lean gives the same data-only lexicographic Gibbs learner, finite-sample bound, and explicit two-branch inversion; the omitted tilde-O sentence is a direct redundant consequence of the explicit n₀ formula.

nl.statement:
Let \(r,g:S\to[0,1]\), put \(\Delta=g-r\), and let \(\pi_r\) and \(\pi_g\) be their Gibbs policies relative to \(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\). Define
\[
A=\mathbb E_{\rho,\pi_r}\Delta^2,
\qquad
B=\mathbb E_{\rho,\pi_g}\Delta^2.
\]
Then
\[
J_{\eta,r}(\pi_r)-J_{\eta,r}(\pi_g)
\le\min\left\{\eta(A+B),\sqrt A+\sqrt B\right\}.
\]

review.note: After unfolding the Gibbs policies and regularized welfare, A and B are exactly the two endpoint Gibbs-weighted squared errors and the conclusion is the stated minimum bound.

nl.statement:
For \(g,f\in\mathcal F\), let
\[
H_{g,f}(x)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\pi_g(a\mid x)\{g(x,a)-f(x,a)\}^2,
\]
where \(\pi_g\) is the Gibbs policy generated by \(g\). Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be independent with law \(\rho\), write \(P_\rho h=\mathbb E_\rho h(X)\) and \(P_nh=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nh(X_i)\), and fix \(0<\zeta<1\). With probability at least \(1-\zeta\), simultaneously for every \(g,f\in\mathcal F\),
\[
P_\rho H_{g,f}\le2P_nH_{g,f}+b_n(\zeta),
\qquad
P_nH_{g,f}\le2P_\rho H_{g,f}+b_n(\zeta),
\]
where
\[
b_n(\zeta)=\frac{8}{3n}\left[\log\frac2\zeta+2d\log\{1+4n(\eta+2)\}\right]+\frac3n.
\]

review.note: The prediction polytope is the paper's bounded linear class, gibbsRadius and the remainder unfold to the displayed formulas, and omitting ζ<1 only adds the automatically true ζ≥1 probability regime.

nl.statement:
Fix \(d\ge4\), \(\eta>0\), and a public experiment \(\mathfrak E=(\mathcal X,\mathcal A,\phi,\pi_{\mathrm{ref}},\eta)\), where the context law \(\rho\) remains law-specific. For every \(1<D\le C<e^\eta\), nonemptiness of \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\) is equivalent to the explicit finite exponential nonlinear-semidefinite system in \(\text{lem:fixed-experiment-shell-certificate}\). Whenever that shell is nonempty, the explicit measurable idealized global-optimization learner of \(\text{thm:clean-temperature-feature-upper}\) uses only \((\mathcal D_n,\mathfrak E)\), not \(\rho\), \(C\), or \(D\). For every \(0<\epsilon<1\), the following inversion holds. If \(\eta\le2\epsilon\), then \(N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=1\). If \(\eta>2\epsilon\), put
\[
q_\epsilon=dD\min\{\eta/\epsilon,\epsilon^{-2}\},
\qquad
\ell_\epsilon=1+\log(eq_\epsilon)+\log\{1+(1+\eta)q_\epsilon\}.
\]
Then
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)
\le\left\lceil10^8q_\epsilon\ell_\epsilon\right\rceil
=\widetilde O\!\left(dD\min\{\eta/\epsilon,\epsilon^{-2}\}\right).
\]
On a nonempty boundary shell, \(N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,1,1,\eta)=1\) for every \(\epsilon>0\). The tuple \((d,C,D,\eta)\) does not determine the fixed-design minimax frontier: for every \(1<D\le C<e^\eta\), there are two finite public experiments \(\mathfrak E_0\) and \(\mathfrak E_1\) having nonempty exact shells at those same indices such that
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E_0}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=1\quad(\epsilon>0),
\]
whereas, for constants \(c(C,D,\eta)>0\) and \(\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)>0\),
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E_1}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)\ge c(C,D,\eta)\frac{dD\eta}{\epsilon}
\quad\text{for }0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta).
\]
The informative construction applies without the condition \(2D-1<e^\eta\), but its constants are pointwise in \((C,D,\eta)\); the invariant lower-rate content is \(\Omega_{C,D,\eta}(d/\epsilon)\), not uniform dependence on \(D\) or \(\eta\). Consequently, uniformly over public experiments, no lower bound based only on \((d,C,D,\eta)\) can exceed one or diverge as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\). For every specified finite experiment with a nonempty exact shell and fixed \((d,C,D,\eta)\),
\[
\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\frac{\epsilon^2}{d}N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=0,
\]
so no positive \(d/\epsilon^2\), or fixed-\(D\) \(dD/\epsilon^2\), lower branch can hold for all sufficiently small \(\epsilon\).

Fix \(d\ge4\), \(\eta>0\), and a public experiment \(\mathfrak E\). Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,C,D,\eta)\) is equivalent to feasibility of one of the finitely many explicit exponential nonlinear-semidefinite systems displayed in \(\text{lem:fixed-experiment-shell-certificate}\). If the boundary shell \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak E}(d,1,1,\eta)\) is nonempty, then \(N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,1,1,\eta)=1\) for every \(\epsilon>0\). Whenever a nontrivial fixed-design shell is nonempty, the explicit measurable idealized global-optimization learner of \(\text{thm:clean-temperature-feature-upper}\) uses only \((\mathcal D_n,\mathfrak E)\), not \(\rho\), \(C\), or \(D\). For every \(0<\epsilon<1\), the following inversion holds. If \(\eta\le2\epsilon\), then \(N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=1\). If \(\eta>2\epsilon\), define
\[
q_\epsilon=dD\min\{\eta/\epsilon,\epsilon^{-2}\},
\qquad
\ell_\epsilon=1+\log(eq_\epsilon)+\log\{1+(1+\eta)q_\epsilon\},
\]
\[
n_0=\left\lceil10^8q_\epsilon\ell_\epsilon\right\rceil.
\]
Then the learner has worst-case expected regularized regret at most \(\epsilon\) at sample size \(n_0\), and
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)\le n_0
=\widetilde O\!\left(dD\min\{\eta/\epsilon,\epsilon^{-2}\}\right).
\]
The tuple \((d,C,D,\eta)\) does not, however, determine the fixed-design minimax frontier. For every \(1<D\le C<e^\eta\), there are finite public experiments \(\mathfrak E_0\) and \(\mathfrak E_1\) with nonempty exact shells at the same indices such that
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E_0}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=1\qquad(\epsilon>0),
\]
whereas, for constants \(c(C,D,\eta)>0\) and \(\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)>0\),
\[
N^\star_{\mathfrak E_1}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)\ge c(C,D,\eta)\frac{dD\eta}{\epsilon}
\qquad(0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_0(C,D,\eta)).
\]
The informative construction includes pairs with \(2D-1\ge e^\eta\), but its constant is pointwise in \((C,D,\eta)\); its invariant content is \(\Omega_{C,D,\eta}(d/\epsilon)\), not uniform lower dependence on \(D\) or \(\eta\). Consequently every lower bound asserted uniformly over all public experiments and based only on \((d,C,D,\eta)\) is at most one. Moreover, for each specified finite experiment with a nonempty exact shell and fixed \((d,C,D,\eta)\),
\[
\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\frac{\epsilon^2}{d}N^\star_{\mathfrak E}(\epsilon;d,C,D,\eta)=0,
\]
so no positive quadratic lower branch can hold throughout all sufficiently small accuracies. Thus the clean upper bound is universal over every nonempty exact shell, while lower matching is only pointwise and local in the \(d/\epsilon\) rate on the constructed informative experiment.

nl.statement:
Let \(r,g:S\to[0,1]\), put \(\Delta=g-r\), and suppose \(\Delta\le0\) pointwise. Write
\[
J_{\eta,r}(\pi)=\mathbb E_{\rho,\pi}r(X,A)-\eta^{-1}\mathbb E_\rho\operatorname{KL}(\pi(\cdot\mid X)\Vert\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid X)).
\]
For \(\gamma\in[0,1]\), let \(\pi_\gamma(\cdot\mid x)\) be the Gibbs policy generated by \(r+\gamma\Delta\), so \(\pi_0=\pi_r\) and \(\pi_1=\pi_g\). Then
\[
J_{\eta,r}(\pi_r)-J_{\eta,r}(\pi_g)
\le\min\left\{\mathbb E_{\rho,\pi_r}[-\Delta],\frac\eta2\mathbb E_{\rho,\pi_r}\Delta^2\right\}.
\]
